claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is an environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service that specifies the domain serving the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
In self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN may be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN, so a separate domain and second DNS record is not required.

The Pulumi Terraform state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses tf.pulumi.com as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the terraform login / tofu login command, and the TF_TOKEN_* variable name.

For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the terraform login or tofu login command, and the TF_TOKEN_* variable name should use the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value in place of tf.pulumi.com.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ documenting the Terraform state backend guide.
